subject: falcon
title: Scientists Found Live Songbirds Stuffed in Rocks Beside Falcon Nests

scenes.text: Scientists found live songbirds jammed into rocks beside falcon nests.
It was on a Moroccan island where Eleonora's falcons breed late, timed to the autumn songbird migration.
The small birds were wedged deep in cracks, some with wing and tail feathers pulled out. All alive.
The researchers think it's a living larder. In dry heat a dead bird dries out. A trapped one stays fresh.
A local fisherman already knew about it.
Not everyone is convinced. Nobody has yet watched a falcon lock a bird in, or come back to eat it.

description:
Live songbirds have been found jammed into rock crevices beside the nests of Eleonora's falcons.
The falcons nest very late, from July to October, so that their breeding season coincides with the autumn migration of small birds. During a 2014 survey on the Mogador archipelago off Essaouira, Morocco, Abdeljebbar Qninba and colleagues found small migrants trapped in deep holes and fissures, some with their flight and tail feathers removed, all still alive; they reported it in the journal Alauda in 2015 and suggested the falcons keep prey alive so it stays fresh. Other ornithologists are cautious: the birds may have escaped and hidden, and no one has yet seen a falcon stash a victim or return to eat it.
Larder or coincidence: what do you think? Comment below.
first_comment: For most of the year these falcons eat insects; they switch to birds only while nesting. Larder or coincidence: what do you think?
